lastCompletedStory.title: Add check:all guard gate forbidding toolchain-version-conditioned skips

openQuestions: During the post-fix full-suite `bun test` run (after the check-all.test.ts / gates-manifest.test.ts updates but before the file-size ratchet fix), exactly one run out of the full sequence reported '1 fail' with no captured test name (the terminal output scrolled past before I isolated it). 23 subsequent full-suite `bun test` re-runs (across several minutes, no further code changes) were all clean (0 fail). I could not identify which test it was or reproduce it again, and nothing in this story's diff (scripts/check-version-skips.ts, check-all.ts GATES entry, the two updated manifest test files, the file-size budget, and the new fixtures) touches Ink/tmux/timing surfaces that are the usual source of this repo's documented flakes (patterns.md CAM-186/CAM-201 mock-terminal-size bullets). Flagging per the no-flaky-evasion rule (CAM-202) rather than silently discarding it: if a similar single-run '1 fail' recurs in CI or a future worker's suite, it is NOT yet root-caused and should not be waved through as 'known flaky' on the strength of this note alone.

The story's acceptance criteria list 'skipUnless' as a skip form the gate must detect, but bun:test's real public API has no `skipUnless` member (confirmed via Step 5.5 WebSearch against bun.com/reference/bun/test/Test/skipIf and bun.com/docs/test/writing-tests: the real forms are `skip`, `skipIf`, `todoIf`, `todo`, `if`, `failing`). The gate treats all four story-named forms (skipIf/skip/skipUnless/todoIf) as pure TEXT patterns (a `.formName(` regex), not runtime-verified bun:test calls, so detecting a nonexistent `skipUnless` costs nothing at scan time; the one fixture exercising it (`process-versions-skipunless.ts`) needed a `// @ts-expect-error` to keep `bun run typecheck` green. If a future bun:test release ever adds a real `skipUnless`, no gate change is needed.
nextStoryContext: US-006 (Add fail-closed container toolchain assert to the preflight layer) is next by priority. It continues the CAM-201 toolchain-parity thread: US-001..US-003 built the toolchain-pin reader (`src/config/toolchain.ts`: readPinnedBunVersion/readPinnedNodeVersion) and wired it into the Dockerfile build-arg path (`buildDockerBuildArgv`'s resolveBunVersion/resolveNodeVersion in `src/supervisor/worker-container.ts`); US-004 removed the only two pre-existing Bun.version-conditioned skips; US-005 (this story) added the `version-skips` gate to the GATES manifest (scripts/check-all.ts, now 11 gates) that permanently forbids reintroducing that anti-pattern in test/. US-006 should look at the container preflight layer (likely `src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts` / container-config.ts precedent, per patterns.md's FirewallError/ContainerConfigError fail-closed-throw convention) and assert the RUNNING container's actual bun/node version matches the pinned versions from `src/config/toolchain.ts`, throwing (fail-closed, no worker dispatch) on mismatch rather than silently drifting -- this is the other half of the cam/pr-66 incident class (the container drifted from the pin without anyone noticing until CI went red).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed via WebSearch (bun.com/reference/bun/test/Test/skipIf + bun.com/docs/test/writing-tests): bun:test's real skip-form API is skip/skipIf/todo/todoIf/if/failing -- there is no real 'skipUnless'. The gate (scripts/check-version-skips.ts) intentionally treats all four story-named forms (skipIf/skip/skipUnless/todoIf) as textual patterns rather than runtime-verified API calls, so this is a documented, deliberate divergence (see openQuestions), not a misunderstanding of the real API; the one fixture using the nonexistent form carries a // @ts-expect-error so bun run typecheck stays green.
